Job Description:

About the Role

HPE Financial Services (HPEFS) is seeking a Senior Program Manager, Strategic Digital Initiatives to lead the business-side execution of a large-scale digital platform program that enables new capabilities, modernizes operations, and improves customer and partner experiences. Reporting to the Digital Strategy Leader, this role is accountable for integrated delivery of the assigned initiative across business, product, operations, technology, data, change management, Finance, and external partner teams.

The Senior Program Manager translates approved strategic objectives into an executable, integrated program plan and drives delivery from planning through platform implementation, launch, stabilization, adoption, and value realization. The role operates within the enterprise product operating model, governance standards, planning cadence, and delivery frameworks established by Product Operations & Governance and the broader Transformation Office.

This position is suited to a leader who thrives in ambiguity, builds alignment across diverse stakeholder groups, and drives disciplined execution in a highly matrixed environment.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Program Leadership

  • Lead integrated business execution for an assigned large-scale digital platform initiative within established enterprise planning and governance frameworks.

  • Develop and maintain the integrated program plan, milestones, success measures, decision log, and cross-workstream delivery plan for the assigned initiative.

  • Monitor scope, schedule, budget, risks, issues, decisions, and dependencies, and drive timely mitigation or escalation.

  • Apply the product operating model, governance standards, planning cadence, and delivery controls defined by Product Operations & Governance and the broader enterprise program.

Business Outcomes and Value Realization

  • Develop and maintain the business case, benefits framework, measurable outcomes, and value realization plan in partnership with Finance and business leaders.

  • Track progress against expected business, customer, partner, and operational outcomes and recommend corrective action when needed.

  • Ensure digital platform investments translate into sustainable operational improvements and measurable value.

Cross-Functional Integration

  • Orchestrate execution across Product Management, Operations, Technology, Data, Process Engineering, Compliance, Finance, Change Management, and external partners.

  • Manage interdependencies across workstreams and establish clear ownership, decision rights, and escalation paths.

  • Facilitate issue resolution and maintain alignment between business priorities and technical delivery.

Product and Business Delivery Alignment

  • Partner with Product Managers, Product Owners, and business leaders to align strategic objectives, customer needs, operational requirements, and delivered platform capabilities.

  • Facilitate initiative-level sequencing and trade-off recommendations based on approved product priorities, business value, risk, readiness, and dependencies; escalate portfolio-level prioritization decisions to the appropriate product and governance leaders.

  • Maintain traceability between program objectives, business requirements, delivered capabilities, and measurable outcomes.

Initiative Governance and Executive Communication

  • Coordinate initiative-level steering committee materials, decision forums, and leadership reviews in alignment with established enterprise governance standards and cadence.

  • Prepare concise executive status updates, decision materials, recommendations, and escalation summaries.

  • Provide transparent reporting on delivery health, value, financials, risks, dependencies, readiness, and decisions.

Vendor and Strategic Partner Management

  • Coordinate day-to-day business-side engagement with implementation partners, consultants, and vendors supporting the assigned initiative.

  • Monitor vendor commitments, deliverables, performance, dependencies, and alignment to program outcomes.

  • Partner with Procurement, Legal, Finance, Technology, and the appropriate business owner on initiative-specific contract deliverables, commercial issues, and value delivery; use established sourcing and RFP frameworks.

Platform Readiness, Launch, and Adoption

  • Coordinate business readiness for platform deployment, including process alignment, data readiness, execution of business testing, training, communications, support models, and adoption planning. Apply the enterprise UAT framework and standards owned by Product Operations & Governance.

  • Partner with Product, Operations, Technology, and Change Management teams to plan go-live, stabilization, and transition to ongoing operations.

  • Monitor adoption, stakeholder feedback, and early-life performance, and drive actions needed to achieve expected outcomes.

Budget and Financial Oversight

  • Manage program budgets, forecasts, funding requirements, and financial reporting for the assigned initiative.

  • Monitor expenditures against approved plans and business case assumptions, identify variances, and recommend corrective action.

  • Support investment governance and responsible stewardship of program resources.

Role Boundaries and Key Partnerships

  • Product Operations & Governance owns the enterprise product operating model, portfolio planning cadence, governance standards, delivery-health framework, product enablement practices, UAT framework, and common RFP standards. This role applies those standards to the assigned initiative and provides timely program data and insights.

  • Product Managers and Product Owners own product vision, roadmap, backlog, feature prioritization, and product acceptance. This role integrates their plans with the broader program and manages cross-workstream dependencies, risks, and milestones.

  • The IT Program Manager owns technical delivery planning and execution. This role owns integrated business delivery, stakeholder alignment, business readiness, vendor coordination, and value realization for the assigned initiative.

  • The broader Transformation Office owns enterprise-level program governance, cross-program integration, and overall transformation outcomes. This role represents and delivers the assigned digital initiative within that structure.

Education and Experience Required

  • First-level university degree or equivalent experience; advanced university degree preferred in Business, Information Systems, Technology, Program Management, or a related field.

  • Typically 8+ years of experience leading complex business, digital, operational, or technology-enabled programs.

  • Demonstrated experience leading enterprise-scale digital platform implementations, modernization programs, or technology-enabled business initiatives involving multiple stakeholders, vendors, and cross-functional teams.

  • Demonstrated success coordinating business, operational, product, technology, data, and vendor stakeholders through implementation, go-live, stabilization, and adoption.

  • Experience developing business cases, managing budgets, establishing governance, and driving value realization.

  • Experience supporting platform selection, implementation, migration, rollout, or operational readiness initiatives preferred.

  • Experience operating in a highly matrixed environment with executive-level stakeholders.

  • Financial services, leasing, banking, fintech, or enterprise technology experience preferred.

Strategic Program Management

Digital Platform Delivery

Enterprise Program Leadership

Cross-Functional Leadership

Executive Stakeholder Management

Governance and Decision Management

Business Case Development

Value Realization

Business Readiness and Adoption

Vendor Implementation Management

Budget and Financial Management

Risk and Dependency Management

Change Management

Product and Business Alignment

Large-Scale System Implementation

Executive Communication

Negotiation and Influencing

Leadership Without Authority

Accountability, Active Listening, Business Acumen, Collaboration, Critical Thinking, Customer Focus, Data-Driven Decision Making, Financial Acumen, Growth Mindset, Influencing Skills, Managing Ambiguity, Outcome-Based Requirements, Prioritization, Program Governance, Relationship Building, Strategic Thinking, and Vendor Management.

title: Rehabilitation Specialist
description:
Rehabilitation Specialist

Vale Hospital | Permanent | Full time

Up to £27,985 per annum depending on experience

37.5 hours per week


At Nuffield Health the UKs largest healthcare charity, everything we give our patients, members and customers would not be possible without you. Your passion, your warmth, your drive to make a difference. Whether it’s driving connected health, helping the nation, transforming experiences, or building the career you want – we give you the support to do it all. Join our journey. It starts with you.


We are looking for a Rehabilitation Specialist to help us build a healthier nation. We are looking for a Rehabilitation Specialist who will deliver Nuffield Health Rehabilitation Programmes utilising the unique Nuffield Health pathway, championing the Charitable Purpose. This role will play a crucial part in Nuffield’s long-term vision for clinical rehabilitation and will require the Rehabilitation Specialist to undertake remote (digital) and in person facilitation of exercise, emotion wellbeing support, healthy eating, and goal setting to aid the participants recovery. The pathway will involve weekly 1to1s, group exercise classes (virtual and in person), promote goal setting and self-directed activity.


You will demonstrate leadership and influencing skills, be a good communicator, organised and self-motived. As part of this role, you will work collaboratively onsite, centrally and with our Charity team and our beneficiaries. You will need excellent IT skills and hold a Level 3 Personal trainer qualification which is essential for the role. Ideally you will have previous experience working in a Rehabilitation Specialist position and an understanding of rehabilitation, along with potentially a Bsc (Hons) in Sports Rehabilitation (desired not essential).


As a Rehabilitation Specialist you will:

  • Organise and run a series of rolling 12-week rehabilitation programmes.
  • Facilitate and deliver both live stream and in person group exercise classes, with people that have varying degrees of abilities and physical function.
  • Be able to promote self-directed activity using pre-recorded on demand classes and a journal which will aid in the participants being able to self-manage their condition after the 12-week Programme.
  • Capability to re-calibrate exercises and intensities based on regular improvements demonstrated by changes in both effort and performance.
  • Identify any deterioration of participants and if necessary follow internal escalation processes, ensuring reporting is processed within a specific timeframe and that outcome data is accurately captured, which is essential in supporting our Charitable Purpose and tracking and monitoring participants progress.

title: Project Manager III

The Project Manager (PM) works collaboratively on projects of varying sizes and complexity. Most projects will require working closely with technical resources and business partners. This role will be engaged during the project process from conception to closure and hand-off to operations. The PM will create and foster lasting positive vendor and customer relationships and expected to work with a cross-functional team consisting of team members from multiple organizations. In this role, the PM must keep the team engaged and focused, remove blockers, and maintain the project schedule, scope and budget.
A person who will be successful in this role will need to be organized, adaptable, and self-motivated. They must be perceptive and able to discern project and task priority with little direction. This person must be able to lead and keep the team on task. Lastly, the ability to quickly understand our business and apply critical thinking skills to the job responsibilities will be very important to success in this role.

  • deployment planning

  • owners/sponsors

title: Specjalista(-ka) ds. procesów kredytowych
description:
Na bank zadbamy dla Ciebie o:

  • umowę o pracę (pierwsza na 12 miesięcy),
  • pracę hybrydową częściowo w biurze w Warszawie, Plac Europejski 3A (przy Rondzie Daszyńskiego), lub w Poznaniu, ul. Kolorowa 8 i 10 (przy centrum handlowym King Cross), lub we Wrocławiu, ul. Robotnicza 11 (przy Muzeum Współczesnym),
  • zespół/lidera: Centre-Chapter Credit Product Management (Paulina Książkiewicz-Żyniewicz | LinkedIn)
  • cel: rozwój i optymalizacja procesów kredytowych dla klientów SME.

Należymy do pierwszej trójki największych banków w Polsce i jesteśmy częścią międzynarodowej Grupy Erste. W naszej centrali łączymy kilkanaście jednostek biznesowych, w tym nasze zaplecze technologiczne. Choć jesteśmy zupełnie różni to mamy jeden cel - wszystko robimy na bank.


Na co dzień pracujemy w metodyce agile - w chapterach i squadach. Mamy też możliwość integracji z innymi pracownikami np. dzięki ponad 20 Klubom Zainteresowań.


Cenimy różnorodność wśród naszych pracowników. Wierzymy, że każdy, bez względu na indywidualne predyspozycje, może wnieść niepowtarzalną perspektywę do naszej firmy.

Aplikuj, jeśli:

  • masz doświadczenie w analizie biznesowej, procesowej lub produktowej,
  • potrafisz przekładać potrzeby biznesu na wymagania funkcjonalne i niefunkcjonalne, masz doświadczenie w tworzeniu user stories, kryteriów akceptacji oraz dokumentacji analitycznej,
  • potrafisz modelować procesy biznesowe i analizować wpływ zmian,
  • znasz metodyki Agile i masz doświadczenie w pracy w zespołach scrumowych,
  • rozumiesz proces wytwarzania oprogramowania oraz rolę poszczególnych uczestników procesu (analityków systemowych, architektów, developerów, testerów),
  • potrafisz współpracować z różnorodnymi interesariuszami,
  • posiadasz umiejętności analityczne i komunikacyjne,
  • znasz język angielski na poziomie umożliwiającym swobodną komunikację.

Mile widziane, jeśli będziesz mieć:

  • znajomość procesów kredytowych lub produktów dla klientów SME,
  • doświadczenie w sektorze bankowym,
  • znajomość BPMN, UML lub innych technik modelowania procesów i wymagań,
  • doświadczenie w pracy z Jira, Confluence lub podobnymi narzędziami,
  • doświadczenie we wspieraniu testów biznesowych i odbiorów użytkowników,
  • znajomość zagadnień związanych z architekturą systemów i integracjami,
  • znajomość narzędzi do modelowania procesów i analizy danych.

Twoje zadania w tej roli:

  • identyfikacja i analiza potrzeb klientów oraz użytkowników procesów kredytowych, w tym prowadzenie analiz biznesowych zgodnie z obowiązującymi standardami i dobrymi praktykami,
  • współpraca z Product Ownerem i zespołami IT przy rozwoju rozwiązań cyfrowych,
  • dbanie o odpowiedni poziom jakości wymagań, umożliwiający sprawne projektowanie rozwiązań systemowych i efektywną realizację prac developerskich,
  • wspieranie zespołu podczas refinementów, planowań, testów oraz odbiorów biznesowych,
  • definiowanie wymagań biznesowych, user stories oraz kryteriów akceptacji, a także przygotowywanie i utrzymywanie dokumentacji analitycznej,
  • udział w projektowaniu oraz optymalizacji ścieżek klienta,
  • analiza danych, monitorowanie efektów wdrożeń i rekomendowanie usprawnień,
  • współpraca z jednostkami biznesowymi, ryzykiem, prawnymi i operacyjnymi,
  • wsparcie wdrożeń nowych produktów i zmian regulacyjnych.

To masz na bank:

  • umowę o pracę (pierwszą na 12 miesięcy),
  • pracę w trybie hybrydowym w (lokalizacja na początku oferty),
  • prywatną opiekę medyczną Medicover (z możliwością wykupienia pakietu stomatologicznego),
  • system kafeteryjny z punktami do wymiany na aktywności, np. wypoczynkowe, kulturalne, gastronomiczne lub dofinansowanie do przedszkola/żłobka/klubu dziecięcego,
  • kartę Multisport,
  • ofertę produktową banku oraz pożyczki na pracowniczych warunkach,
  • aktywności wellbeingowe, np. Kluby Zainteresowań, webinary, ćwiczenia, podcasty; inicjatywy w biurach np. mammobus, profilaktyczne badanie wzroku, warsztaty z samoobrony,
  • wyprawkę dla dzieci,
  • benefity dla osób z niepełnosprawnościami: dodatek finansowy na cele prozdrowotne, dodatkowe 2 dni urlopu dla pracowników z lekkim stopniem niepełnosprawności, całkowita praca zdalna, jeśli charakter pracy na to pozwala,
  • platformę ze szkoleniami zewnętrznymi i wewnętrznymi – np. programowanie czy analiza danych lub komunikacja, podejście strategiczne, negocjacje i inne,
  • program poleceń pracowniczych – nagrodę pieniężną za polecenie osoby do pracy w banku.

Jak wygląda wdrożenie i rozwój?

  • Na bank nie rzucimy Cię na głęboką wodę. Zaplanowaliśmy wdrożenie, które obejmować będzie wprowadzenie do organizacji, Twojej jednostki biznesowej i zadań.
  • Przez początkowy okres pracy będzie towarzyszył Ci Buddy, który pokaże Ci naszą kulturę organizacyjną i odpowie na wszystkie pytania.

Dołącz do nas w kilku krokach.

  • Wyślij CV do naszej analizy, a my podejmiemy decyzję czy zaprosimy Cię do kolejnego etapu.
  • Spotkaj się (online) z rekruterem(-ką) i managerem(-ką).
  • Wykonaj zadanie merytoryczne/test (w zależności od stanowiska).
  • Pracuj z nami w naszym zespole!

Po każdym z etapów rekrutacji otrzymasz od nas informację zwrotną, dostosowaną do jego poziomu zaawansowania. Po spotkaniach zaś wrócimy do Ciebie z kompleksowym podsumowaniem mailowym lub telefonicznym.

Stosujemy najwyższe standardy zarządzania ryzykiem, dbamy o bezpieczeństwo naszych klientów i świadczonych usług.

title: Play Invention Digital Internship
description:
Job Description

Are You an Aspiring Toy Inventor Looking to Discover New Play?

Join the LEGO® Group’s Play Discovery team within the Creative Play Lab for a Paid Internship at our Head Quarters in Billund, Denmark!

Are you driven by an unquenchable passion for discovering new play opportunities through early-stage ideation, concept development, and prototyping? If so, you could be one of the talented students joining our Play Discovery department this year, where creativity and imagination thrive!

Start date: September 2026

Length: 4 months (until end of December 2026)

About us:

Creative Play Lab is an ambitious, future‑focused innovation hub inventing radical new play opportunities and never‑seen‑before experiences for LEGO® fans of today and tomorrow. We grow the boundaries of what play can become, using bold experimentation, advanced technologies, and deep insight into how kids play to imagine meaningful, next‑generation experiences. Our mix of creatives, innovators, researchers, engineers, and technologists rapidly transforms curiosity into tangible concepts, redefining the future of play and ensuring LEGO® play remains at the forefront of creativity and joyful exploration.

As an intern in our Play Discovery department, you’ll join teams dedicated to letting loose their creative curiosity and exploring new play experiences. You’ll unleash your imagination across a range of innovation missions, collaborating cross-functionally to develop concepts into playable prototypes.

About the Internship:

We look for interns who bring something genuinely different to our innovation hub, adding fresh cultural insight, creative energy, and new ways of thinking. Your time with us will span personal curiosity projects, team capability-building initiatives, and innovation Missions. Every day is different and you’ll learn directly from a world‑class multidisciplinary team as you build your craft, embracing ambiguity as you discover new play experiences.

Meet the Play Invention Physical team:

The Play Invention Physical team work across many media with materials like plastic, paper, card, wood and textiles to cut, glue and stitch together physical prototypes to visualise and test play. They start with a blank canvas and use physical models, paper sketches, CAD and 3D printing to design new elements that can unlock the next great physical play experience.

Internship Eligibility:

To qualify for this internship opportunity, you must meet all of the following criteria: (1) You will be a student for the full duration of the internship period; (2) You are currently due to graduate after 31st December 2026; (3) You will not be requesting a delayed graduation date to qualify for this internship; (4) This internship will contribute quantitatively towards your course credit and is a compulsory part of your education; (5) You are available to undertake this internship contract starting from 1st September 2026 and ending on 31st December 2026 in Billund, Denmark.

We also encourage interns to have experience with at least some of the following:

  • Sketching

  • Painting

  • Sculpture

  • Woodwork

  • Graphic Design

  • LEGO® Model Building

  • Textiles

  • Machine Workshop tools e.g. lathe, drills etc.

  • Electronics

  • 3D CAD programs

  • Game Engines

  • Coding

  • Videography / Editing

What we’re looking for:

Curiosity: Our teams thrive on a playful curiosity in all they do. You need to be always asking questions, seeking the reason “why”, digging for answers even when it’s hard and never stop wondering “what if...”

Bravery: Our organisation is a huge place full of different people and different perspectives. You need to be comfortable meeting new people every day, speaking up when you disagree, receiving feedback, facing the unknowns of innovation head on and forging yourself a path when things aren’t well defined.

Focus: Our workload and priorities are always changing. You need to be happy shifting priorities fast, focusing on a high priority task one week then focusing on developing your own independent curiosities the next.

Team work: Our best ideas come when we have an amazing rapport with our colleagues and we can collaborate in a respectful and energising way. You need to be at home bouncing ideas off others and building upon the unique contributions and perspectives of your colleagues to create something bigger and better than the sum of its parts. You also need to be encouraging, supportive and empathetic to the fact that different teammates will have different viewpoints and opinions.

Responsibilities:

We want you to bring all your energy, enthusiasm and experiences to work every day so we can achieve amazing things together while you learn along the way. Some of your typical responsibilities could include...

  • Brainstorm a range of possible physical prototypes with a small team to explore how to integrate new materials or functions into physical play

  • Use your making skills to problem solve a particular physical challenge

  • Design and make physical elements that can fulfil a particular purpose or function within a prototype

Perks:

  • Work with a passionate multi-disciplinary team of like-minded creative inventors where you’ll learn something new every day and build your professional network

  • Live and work in the global headquarters of the LEGO® Group in Billund, Denmark and explore our state-of-the-art campus

  • Be an active co-creator with kids – they know how to make fun and meaningful play.

Application:

We welcome international applications for this role however you must be able to live and work in Billund, Denmark for the duration of the internship itself. The LEGO® Group will provide support with permits to work in Denmark for the internship period and we can support with finding accommodation. The costs of your accommodation along with your travel costs to/from Denmark must be covered by you.

We have multiple Play Discovery internships available, each supporting a different team with their own focus area. Take a moment to review all these opportunities and apply only to those that truly align with your strengths. If you have broad skills, applying to more than one team is acceptable but applying to a large number of teams doesn’t increase your chances of making a successful application and makes it harder for us to understand where you’d shine. Please be thoughtful in your approach.

Please ensure your application is completed in English.

To apply, simply submit the following by Saturday 25th April 2026. Please do not risk missing this deadline as we will not consider late applications for this role.

Please attach the following items to your application as 4 separate .PDF documents. Applications failing to do this shall not be considered.

  • An A4 size poster (landscape) designed by you to showcase why you think you are a good fit for the internship. You may use text, photographs, colour etc. to communicate your enthusiasm, talent and values.

  • A current CV detailing your education and relevant experiences.

  • A full portfolio showcasing a more in-depth range of your work. This should include projects that highlight your interests, reflect your passions and demonstrate your hobbies.

  • A bespoke cover letter (no more than 200 words) that tells us what motivates you to apply for this internship and why you think you’re best suited for the placement. If you can do or say something to help your cover letter stand out then please do. We encourage you to be original and authentic to who you are.

Come and join us as we discover the future of play!

Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis. However, please note we do amend or withdraw our jobs and reserve the right to do so at any time, including prior to any advertised closing date. So, if you're interested in this role we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

What’s in it for you?

Here is what you can expect:

Family Care Leave - We offer enhanced paid leave options for those important times.

Insurances – All colleagues are covered by our life and disability insurance which provides protection and peace of mind.

Wellbeing - We want our people to feel well and thrive. We offer resources and benefits to nurture physical and mental wellbeing along with opportunities to build community and inspire creativity.

Colleague Discount – We know you'll love to build, so from day 1 you will qualify for our generous colleague discount.

Bonus - We do our best work to succeed together. When goals are reached and if eligible, you'll be rewarded through our bonus scheme.

Workplace - When you join the team you'll be assigned a primary workplace location i.e. one of our Offices, stores or factories. Our hybrid work policy means an average of 3 days per week in the office. The hiring team will discuss the policy and role eligibility with you during the recruitment process.

Children are our role models. Their curiosity, creativity and imagination inspire everything we do. We strive to create a diverse, dynamic and inclusive culture of play at the LEGO Group, where everyone feels safe, valued and they belong.

The LEGO Group is highly committed to equal employment opportunity and equal pay and seeks to encourage applicants from all backgrounds (eg. sex, gender identity or expression, race/ethnicity, national origin, sexual orientation, disability, age and religion) to apply for roles in our team.

The LEGO Group is fully committed to Children’s Rights and Child Wellbeing across the globe. Candidates offered positions with high engagement with children are required to take part in Child Safeguarding Background Screening, as a condition of the offer.

Thank you for sharing our global commitment to Children’s Rights.

title: Chemical Operator
description:
Solenis is a leading global provider of water and hygiene solutions. The company’s product portfolio includes a broad array of water treatment chemistries, process aids, functional additives, cleaners, disinfectants, and state-of-the-art monitoring, control and delivery systems. These technologies are used by customers to improve operational efficiencies, enhance product quality, protect plant assets, minimize environmental impact, and create cleaner and safer environments. Headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware, the company has 78 manufacturing facilities strategically located around the globe and employs a team of over ~23000 professionals in >160 countries across six continents. Solenis is a 2025 Best Managed Company Gold Standard honoree.

For additional information about Solenis, please visit www.solenis.com or follow us on social media.

Provides technical support to engineers to achieve improvements in cycle-time, yield, unit cost, quality, safety and compliance of production and operations processes | Monitors instruments and equipment and collects operating data, including calibration, inspection, testing and repair activities, to assist in making on-line adjustments to instruments, equipment or products | Analyzes and resolves malfunctions and deviations of instruments and control systems to identify and resolve problems | Conducts analyses and prepares reports using metrics from salvage tracking, trending, reporting and root-cause analyses | Maintains process designs to optimize process and facility use while conforming to standard operating procedures (SOPs) and Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs)

POSITION SUMMARY

Chemical Operator is responsible for safely preparing, weighing, charging, mixing, and processing raw materials according to established procedures in a chemical manufacturing environment. This role ensures batches are mixed to specification, equipment is operated safely, documentation is accurate, and production targets are met. Chemical Operator follows strict safety, quality, and housekeeping standards and works closely with Production, Quality, and Maintenance teams. To be successful in the role, Operator III needs to be safety-focused, detail-oriented, and comfortable working in a fast paced, process-driven environment. Located at our Fort Scott, KS site, Operator III reports to the Plant Manager with direction given by the Operator Lead.

POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES

A Chemical Operator is responsible for but not limited to the following:

Batch Preparation & Mixing Operations

  • Independently measures, stages, and charges raw materials, chemicals, and additives according to batch sheets, formulas, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for all Production lines.
  • Operates mixers, blenders, reactors, pumps, scales, and related processing equipment.
  • Monitors and adjusts mixing parameters (speed, temperature, time, viscosity, pH, etc.) to meet product specifications.
  • Records process information and maintain accurate batch documentation.

Equipment Operation & Monitoring

  • Starts, operates, monitors, and shuts down equipment safely in accordance with training and established procedures.
  • Inspects equipment for abnormalities and takes care of any Maintenance issues.
  • Performs basic equipment cleaning and changeover tasks as required.
  • Follows lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures when necessary.

Safety, Health & Environmental Compliance

  • Follows all plant safety rules, PPE requirements, chemical handling procedures, and environmental guidelines.
  • Handles hazardous materials in accordance with SDS requirements and training.
  • Participates in safety meetings, inspections, and incident reporting.
  • Maintains a clean, organized workspace using 5S and housekeeping standards.

Quality Control & Documentation

  • Performs in‑process checks (temperature, appearance, viscosity, pH, weight, etc.) to confirm batches meet specifications.
  • Collects and labels samples and does quality testing as needed.
  • Documents all required production information accurately and completely.
  • Notifies the Lead or Quality Manager immediately of deviations or irregularities.

POSITION REQUIREMENTS

  • High School diploma or equivalent
  • Chemical Operator certification 1 & 2 or comparable technical training/experience in manufacturing
  • At least 5 years of experience working in a chemical or industrial manufacturing environment.
  • Can be fully trained to operate all lines on the Production floor
  • Some Experience with PLC – controlled equipment, batch processing, or automated systems
  • Experience with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), ISO standards, Kosher, Halaa, and NSF Quality Standards
  • Physical requirements
    • Ability to remain stationary, move, climb stairs and ladders for extended periods during 8–10 hour shifts
    • Ability to lift, push, pull, and carry up to 50 lbs (with assistance for heavier loads)
    • Frequent bending, stooping, kneeling, reaching, and manual valve operation requiring manual dexterity.
    • Ability to work in elevated areas, confined spaces, and on grated platforms
    • Sufficient vision, hearing, and color recognition to read instruments, respond to alarms, and identify hazards
    • Ability to wear required PPE, including chemical‑resistant clothing and respiratory protection, for extended periods
    • Ability to work in hot, cold, noisy, and outdoor environments with exposure to chemicals and odors
    • Physical stamina to work rotating shifts, weekends, holidays, and respond to emergency situations
    • Unable to wear contact lenses

title: Insulator
description:
As a global pioneer in oil-free centrifugal chiller technology with an expanding portfolio of thermal management solutions, Smardt is dedicated to delivering high-efficiency and energy-saving systems for industries, real estate developments, health care and educational centers worldwide.


We operate manufacturing facilities in the US, Canada, Germany, China, and Australia, with a team of over 900 employees. With a focus on reliability, performance, and environmental stewardship, Smardt continues to redefine industry standards through advanced engineering and a commitment to a more sustainable future.


What We're Looking For:

The Insulator is responsible for installing insulation materials on pressure vessels, piping systems, compressors, pumps, heat exchangers, and other mechanical components used in the manufacturing of Smardt chillers and related equipment. This role ensures insulation is accurately measured, cut, fitted, and installed to meet engineering specifications, quality standards, and production requirements while supporting product performance, energy efficiency, and appearance.


The Insulator works closely with Manufacturing, Mechanical Assembly, Boiler Shop, Refrigeration, and Quality teams to ensure insulation activities are completed safely, efficiently, and according to production schedules.


What You'll Do:

  • Measure, cut, shape, and install insulation materials on pressure vessels, piping systems, compressors, pumps, and related equipment.
  • Apply insulation materials using approved adhesives, fastening systems, tapes, and installation methods.
  • Inspect insulation installations to verify fitment, workmanship, appearance, and compliance with specifications.
  • Ensure insulation is properly fitted around complex equipment, geometries and mechanical assemblies.
  • Trim and finish insulation materials to achieve a clean and professional appearance.
  • Handle, store, and use insulation materials, adhesives, and supplies in accordance with manufacturer's recommendations and safety requirements.
  • Maintain tools, equipment, and workstations in clean and organized conditions.
  • Support general production activities as required.
  • Assist with material preparation and movement of equipment and components.
  • Identify and report quality concerns, material shortages, equipment issues, or safety hazards.
  • Follow all company safety procedures, work instructions, and housekeeping standards.
  • Participate in continuous improvement initiatives focused on quality, efficiency, and workplace safety.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned


What You'll Bring


Experience

  • Previous experience in insulation installation, manufacturing, assembly, construction, HVAC, or industrial environments considered an asset.
  • Experience insulating piping systems, pressure vessels, refrigeration equipment, or industrial machinery.
  • Experience working in a manufacturing environment.
  • Ability to lift, carry, push, and pull materials and equipment up to 50 lbs (23 kg).
  • Ability to stand, walk, bend, kneel, crouch, reach, and perform repetitive tasks throughout the workday.
  • Ability to safely use hand tools, cutting tools, adhesives, and insulation materials.
  • Ability to work in a manufacturing environment while wearing required PPE.
  • Ability to work overtime or shift work as required to support production needs.


Education / Certifications

  • High School Diploma or equivalent.
  • An equivalent combination of education and related experience may be considered.


Technical Skills

  • Strong understanding of geometry, measurements, and spatial fitment.
  • Ability to accurately measure, cut, shape, and install insulation materials.
  • Knowledge of adhesives and installation techniques.
  • Good mechanical aptitude and manual dexterity.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality workmanship.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills.
  • Ability to adapt to changing priorities and production schedules.
  • A team-oriented mindset with a willingness to support production activities.
  • Ability to maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills in English and/or French.
  • Safety-conscious with a strong commitment to workplace health and safety.


What We Offer:

  • Competitive salary + annual performance bonus
  • 100% employer-paid medical and dental benefits as of day 1!
  • Tele-Health service paid by the employer.
  • Retirement savings plan with employer contributions up to 6%
  • Dynamic team within a high-growth company
  • Company events and team-building activities
  • Ongoing training and professional development opportunities

description:
About the Company
Embitel Technologies is a Volkswagen AG (VW) Group Company. VW is a German multinational automotive manufacturing corporation headquartered in Wolfsburg, Germany. VW is one of the world’s largest automaker by sales. VW sold 10.9 million vehicles in 2019. The group comprises of 12 brands from seven European Countries: Volkswagen, Audi, Lamborghini, Porsche, Bugatti, Bentley, Ducati (motorcycles), Skoda, SEAT, Scania, MAN and Volkswagen commercial vehicles.

About CARIAD (Car, I Am Digital)


The automotive industry is in disruption. As a company, CARIAD is playing a part in multiple large trends at the same time: electrification, automation, and digitalization. The new name builds on changing customer needs. Automotive customers are demanding more comfort, more safety, more sustainability, and more connectivity. With its software platforms and digital features, CARIAD is developing solutions and products that will turn the car into a smart companion to accompany customers into the future with continuous updates and new digital features, even years later. The new company name reflects this zeitgeist: ‘Car, I Am Digital’. The brand profile can be found on its new website .


Currently, around 4,000 employees are working at CARIAD on the digital transformation of the car. CARIAD is working intensively on the software and technology platform for Premium Platform Electric (PPE). The first vehicles based on PPE will be the electric Porsche Macan and Audi Q6 e-tron. At the core of CARIAD is the development of the unified and scalable software and technology platform E³ 2.0 for all Group brands. E³ stands for ‘end to end electronics architecture’. The new software and technology platform is built from scratch and will be used first at the end of 2024 in Artemis, the lighthouse project of Audi. As of 2026, E³ 2.0 is due to be scaled by the Volkswagen brand with Trinity in the volume segment.


About our Group


CARIAD COE (Centre of Excellence) is setup in Bangalore, India working exclusively with CARIAD and associated VW groups with the focus on development of ‘VW.OS”. The areas of work involve development of platform components such as firmware, boot loaders, AUTOSAR, Linux/QNX BSP, Service oriented architecture-based middleware components.

Job Description:

· Extensive hands-on experience in MCAL configuration and integration.

· Strong experience in AUTOSAR Classic BSW Development and Configuration.

· Strong understanding of MCU peripherals, registers, interrupt handling, memory mapping, and multicore architecture.

· Strong experience with at least one of the latest-generation automotive MCU families:

o Infineon AURIX TC4x (Highly Preferred)

o Infineon AURIX TC3xx

o TI C2000

o STM Stellar SR6 P6

· Hands-on experience with AUTOSAR configuration tools, including:

o EB Tresos Studio.

o Vector DaVinci Configurator / DaVinci Developer.

· Good understanding of automotive communication protocols, including:

o CAN/CAN FD/ FlexRay / LIN

· Strong Embedded C programming skills with a focus on automotive embedded systems.

· Proven debugging and troubleshooting skills using:

o Lauterbach TRACE32

o Hardware debuggers

o Diagnostic logs

o Hardware traces

· Strong analytical, problem-solving, and integration skills with the ability to work effectively in a cross-functional automotive software development environment.

Key Responsibilities

· Perform MCAL configuration and integration with strong hands-on expertise.

· Apply strong knowledge of Functional Safety (ISO 26262 Part 6), including MPU, BIST, redundant core memory configuration, and safety-compliant software development practices.

· Configure and integrate the following AUTOSAR/MCAL modules:

o MCAL (DIO, Timer, Clock)

o GPT / ICU / PWM

o ADC

o SPI and I2C

o CAN / CAN FD / FlexRay

o DMA

o WDG Timer

o Flash / EEPROM

· Execute ECU configuration, code generation, BSW integration, build, and validation activities.

· Configure MCU-specific features, including:

o CDD development and integration for eConverter (DCDC and OBC)

o Clock configuration

o Interrupt configuration

o Memory configuration

o Multicore configuration

o Watchdog configuration

o DMA configuration

o Peripheral configuration

o Reset and start-up configuration

· Debug BSW and MCAL integration issues and perform root cause analysis at the register, driver, and hardware levels.

· Develop, configure, and integrate AUTOSAR Basic Software (BSW) modules.

· Collaborate closely with hardware, application software, system integration, and validation teams to ensure successful ECU delivery.

title: Senior Plant Operator
location: Suffolk, Virginia, United States of America
description:
Solenis is a leading global provider of water and hygiene solutions. The company’s product portfolio includes a broad array of water treatment chemistries, process aids, functional additives, cleaners, disinfectants, and state-of-the-art monitoring, control and delivery systems. These technologies are used by customers to improve operational efficiencies, enhance product quality, protect plant assets, minimize environmental impact, and create cleaner and safer environments. Headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware, the company has 78 manufacturing facilities strategically located around the globe and employs a team of over ~23000 professionals in >160 countries across six continents. Solenis is a 2025 Best Managed Company Gold Standard honoree.

For additional information about Solenis, please visit www.solenis.com or follow us on social media.


The VFA Senior Plant Operator will apply advanced technical knowledge and operational expertise to support safe and efficient production. This role will work closely with other shifts and site departments such as: Maintenance, Lab, Engineering, and Material Handling to maximize equipment performance and ensure production targets are met. The position is responsible for meeting production goals, while maintaining high safety and environmental performance.

This role will support the commissioning and startup of a new plant on site. While the role will eventually transition to a rotating 12-hour shift schedule, the first 1–2 years will be worked on a Monday–Friday daytime schedule.


Principal Accountabilities

  • Operate plant to meet productivity targets and handle chemicals charges in a safe manner as defined by standard procedures.
  • Monitor process and adjust control parameters with the control systems
  • Conduct routine rounds and actively participate in shift turnover
  • Maintain process control to ensure First Pass Quality is achieved
  • Perform a complete and detailed turnover and ensure that all required documentation is complete and accurate
  • Maintain and restock supplies and raw materials as necessary for the assigned process area
  • Ability to lift 55 pounds, excessive walking, bending, continuous climbing of stairs, operate a forklift and cleaning equipment
  • Maintain high standards of housekeeping in work area
  • Serve as process expert in safety reviews
  • Be actively involved in Safety Programs in any of the following roles: auditor, implementer of corrective actions, attend meetings, etc. Train others to have familiarity with these programs (OEL, Safety audits, Site Safety Committee, 5S, regulator audits, etc.)
  • Ability to follow written and verbal instructions with minimal direct supervision to meet daily goals
  • Understand and operate within Federal and State regulations pertaining to safety and environmental requirements (EPA programs, RCRA and DOT) and OSHA
  • Other duties as assigned/requested

Success Criteria

  • Ability to recognize hazards and change behaviors to support a Zero incident mindset for self and others
  • Achieving stated throughput targets in accordance to the production schedule, while maintaining safety, quality, and productivity rates
  • Ability to complete the site Hazwoper certification and join the Emergency Response Team, perform duties in all types of PPE up to an incapsulated suit, able to work in confined spaces and not afraid of heights.
  • Stay clean shaven for respirator usage
  • Ability to operate within a high paced, team-focused production area and continually progress to learn all aspects of the plant
  • Have a full working knowledge of the equipment and processes associated with the plant and packaging
  • Pursue all aspects of waste minimization to ensure products are properly disposition, and understanding the waste process to handle generation as regulated
  • Ability to understand and operate the plant within Federal and State regulations pertaining to Waste management (EPA programs, RCRA and DOT) and OSHA

Qualifications

  • High School diploma, proficient in math, written and spoken English
  • Strong knowledge of hazardous chemical handling
  • Strong communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to follow direction and communicate across multiple departments

Preferred knowledge/skills

  • Deep understanding and experience with chemical manufacturing process equipment including reactors, distillation columns, and automation.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office, Distributed Control Systems/PLCs (DeltaV), and Data Historians

title: Compliance and Quality Lead
description:
Compliance and Quality Lead

This role has been designed as 'Hybrid' with a requirement that you will work on average 2 days per week from an HPE office.

Who We Are:

Hewlett Packard Enterprise is the global edge-to-cloud company advancing the way people live and work. We help companies connect, protect, analyze, and act on their data and applications wherever they live, from edge to cloud, so they can turn insights into outcomes at the speed required to thrive in today’s complex world. Our culture thrives on finding new and better ways to accelerate what’s next. We know varied backgrounds are valued and succeed here. We have the flexibility to manage our work and personal needs. We make bold moves, together, and are a force for good. If you are looking to stretch and grow your career our culture will embrace you. Open up opportunities with HPE.

Job Description:

The Compliance and Quality Lead is responsible for establishing, maintaining, and continuously improving compliance, information security, and quality management processes and practices across the Managed Services Delivery (MSD) organization. The role leads internal and external assessments and certification activities related to ISO 27001, TISAX, SOC 1 (ISAE 3402), SOC 2, ISO 20000, and other applicable industry standards and regulatory requirements.

The Compliance and Security Lead ensures compliance with internal policies, customer obligations, and industry best practices, while driving continuous improvement initiatives related to information security, IT risk management, service quality, and operational excellence.


How you will make your mark:

  • Develop, implement, maintain, and continuously improve management systems and governance frameworks supporting ISO 27001, ISO 20000, TISAX, SOC 1 (ISAE 3402), SOC 2, and other applicable standards.
  • Own and coordinate certification and recertification activities, customer assessments, including preparation, execution, and follow-up actions.
  • Plan and lead internal audits, assessments, and compliance reviews.
  • Develop, maintain, and improve policies, procedures, standards, work instructions, and process documentation.
  • Identify compliance gaps, audit findings, and nonconformities; drive corrective and preventive actions through closure.
  • Manage compliance and operational risk processes and ensure effective mitigation plans are established and tracked.
  • Monitor the effectiveness of compliance and quality controls and recommend improvements based on industry best practices.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on process efficiency, service quality, customer satisfaction, and operational excellence.
  • Review business requirements and ensure processes, controls, and documentation are updated accordingly.
  • Maintain accurate records of process changes, audit results, certifications, risk assessments, and corrective actions.
  • Develop and maintain compliance and quality metrics, dashboards, and reports for management reviews.
  • Collaborate effectively with delivery teams, customers, auditors, and stakeholders to ensure compliance, security and quality objectives are achieved.
  • Deliver awareness sessions, training, and guidance related to compliance, quality management, and organizational standards.
  • Support customer due diligence activities and compliance-related requests.
  • Lead, coordinate and participate in team internal projects, organizational improvement, internal and external events and quality management initiatives.
  • Support Delivery in achieving business objectives

About you:

  • Relevant professional experience in IT compliance, information security, audit, risk management, quality management, or related discipline.
  • Excellent leadership and communication skills.
  • Experience with one or more of the following frameworks and standards:

ISO 27001

ISO 20000

TISAX

SOC 1 (ISAE 3402)

SOC 2

  • Excellent planning and organizational skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously and prioritize effectively.
  • Good understanding of Managed Services operations and IT service delivery processes.
  • Excellent communication and influencing skills with the ability to engage stakeholders at all organizational levels.
  • Proactive and self-motivated, with the ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English.
  • Excellent documentation, reporting, and record-management skills.
  • High attention to detail and commitment to quality and compliance standards.
  • Ability to build productive working relationships with customers, auditors, and internal teams.

description:

The Department of Environmental Protection, Bureau of Water Quality, Division of Water Quality Management, is seeking to fill an Environmental Specialist III vacancy in Augusta, Maine.

DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION


ENVIRONMENTAL SPECIALIST III



-ANTICIPATED VACANCY-



Opening Date: September 25, 2026

Closing Date: End of the day October 16, 2026

Location: Augusta

Position Number: 08330-1279

Position Type: Full Time/Year-Round

Class Code: 9253

Grade: 23 (Professional/Technical Unit)

Salary: $25.43 - $35.68 Per Hour*

*(This includes a 7.33% Salary Adjustment). This is earning potential over the course of nine steps; new hires start at step one. Annual step increases are based on performance reviews and authorization of such increases.


Interested candidates need to submit a Direct Hire Application, along with a Cover Letter, and a detailed Resume*


*For us to properly determine if you meet the minimum qualifications for any posting, you must be sure your resume includes the month and year for any relevant experience listed. Your resume should include the duties and responsibilities associated with each position. Any experience that was not full-time employment should be identified as such.


BRIEF JOB DESCRIPTION: The position is primarily responsible for administering the Maine DEP Overboard Discharge (OBD) Compliance Inspection Program and ensuring that approximately 649 licensed OBD systems are properly installed, operated, and maintained in accordance with their licenses and applicable Department requirements throughout the State. The position works with OBD license holders, contract operators, municipal and public officials, and Department staff throughout the life cycle of each system, from licensing and renewal through operation, compliance, enforcement, and eventual removal.


MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Conduct and manage the annual OBD compliance inspection program, including planning and conducting on-site and offshore inspections, investigating complaints, documenting findings, and coordinating follow-up activities.
  • Direct, train, and oversee seasonal Conservation Aides responsible for supporting the OBD inspection program, including participation in their seasonal hiring, training, and assignment of field work.
  • Monitor and manage OBD compliance, including review and maintenance of compliance data, Discharge Monitoring Reports, and preparation of compliance and enforcement actions.
  • Provide technical assistance and regulatory guidance to OBD permit holders and contract operators regarding system operation, maintenance, permit requirements, corrective actions, and system removal.
  • Maintain and administer OBD program records and systems, including inspection and compliance data in the Maine Enterprise Licensing System, and coordinate with the Licensing and Enforcement Units to support effective implementation of the OBD program.

For more information on the specifics of the position, please contact Ben Pendleton at: (207) 592-6871.


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: A six (6) year combination of education and/or experience in environmental, biological, physical science, or engineering which includes two (2) years of environmental experience. Qualifying education must include at least 15 credit hours of science or engineering coursework from an accredited educational institution.


Preference will be given to candidates with the following skills or experience:

  • Experience/knowledge of the design and operations of overboard discharge systems, wastewater treatment plants or traditional subsurface septic systems.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to independently manage a statewide inspection program, prioritize competing responsibilities, and meet regulatory and reporting deadlines.
  • Experience conducting regulatory compliance inspections.
  • Knowledge of water quality laws and regulations.
  • Knowledge of water pollution issues.
  • Ability to understand and follow verbal and written instructions and manage multiple projects.
  • Ability to communicate effectively verbally and in writing.
  • Ability to work independently in remote or challenging locations.
  • Demonstrated skill identifying and resolving issues through collaboration across disciplines to support a high-functioning team.

Currently, this position is not eligible for visa sponsorships or STEM OPT extensions.

title: Field Testing Specialist
description:
Join Vylor—Powering the Future of Agriculture​

At Vylor, we’re advancing agriculture through breakthrough science—combining elite germplasm, cutting-edge biotech, and next-generation expertise in gene editing and molecular breeding. Our portfolio includes trusted industry brands like Pioneer®, Brevant®, and Hoegemeyer®, delivering performance farmers rely on.​

Join us to help scale innovation globally and shape what’s next in crop science.

We are seeking a Field Testing Specialist to join our team. As a Field Testing Specialist, you will be a key contributor for a variety of activities at the Moorhead, MN Research Center. You will play a key role in supporting all projects at the research center through activities including experiment planning, data collection and analysis, and field operations including planting, pollinating and harvest.

Responsibilities – What You’ll Do:

  • Use technology, including drones, iPad, and modern software tools to conduct field research experiments.
  • Follow specific protocols to collect, analyze and distribute large volumes of data.
  • Collaborate with experiment managers to summarize results of experiments, note problem areas during data collection, and recommend actions.
  • Effectively communicate with growers, coworkers, key customers, and management.
  • Assist with research center projects and research seed production activities, including seed preparation for planting, pollinating, and combine/hand harvest. These are critical times for the success of the research program, so weekend work and overtime will be required at these times.
  • Operate agricultural research equipment. This includes tractors, planters, sprayers, forklifts, and research combines.
  • Assist with weed management at our research locations, including spraying and fertilizing operations, ensuring optimal plant health and compliance with environmental regulations.
  • May manage and direct the work of temporary and seasonal employees.
  • Contribute to maintaining a safe and respectful work environment.
  • Provide support for other research projects as assigned.
  • Validate, operate and troubleshoot agricultural research equipment. This includes sprayers, tractors, planters, and combines.
  • Uphold Corteva Agriscience’s Core Values in all aspects of your work, serving as a role model for ethical and professional behavior.

Qualifications – What You’ll Bring:

  • Education: Bachelor’s or master’s degree in agriculture or scientific field with 0-4 years. Experience in agronomy, Biology, Plant Breeding, or a scientific-related field
  • Technologically Savvy: Competency with standard Microsoft Office programs and capacity to learn new technologies and software. Handling of large volumes of data will be required.
  • Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong interpersonal skills. Ability to develop a working relationship with team members by exhibiting effective communication and personal interaction skills with a diverse group of people.
  • Results Driven: Self-motivated and ability to initiate projects, improvements, decisions, and problem solving. Detail-oriented, strong time management and organizational skills.
  • Safety Oriented: Commitment to excellent safety and risk management practices

Physical Requirements:

  • Will be required to do physical lifting and work outdoors and in varying ergonomic environments. Must be capable of lifting 50 pounds.
  • Willing and able to work a flexible schedule including shift work and overtime hours including weekend work required during seasonal peaks.
  • Additional hours and weekends during seasonal peak periods, including some overnight stays.
  • Driver’s License, acceptable driving record, and ability to obtain CMV
  • Ability to obtain FAA Part 107 drone license.
  • Ability to obtain appropriate pesticide applicator license/certification.

*Please note there is no visa sponsorship or relocation assistance available.

Ready to grow your perspective, impact, and career? We seek applicants from all backgrounds to ensure we get the best, most creative talent on our team. Start by applying for this opportunity today.

Benefits – How We’ll Support You:

  • Numerous development opportunities offered to build your skills
  • Be part of a company with a higher purpose and contribute to making the world a better place
  • Health benefits for you and your family on your first day of employment
  • Four weeks of paid time off and two weeks of well-being pay per year, plus paid holidays
  • Excellent parental leave which includes a minimum of 16 weeks for mother and father
  • Future planning with our competitive retirement savings plan and tuition reimbursement program
  • Learn more about our total rewards package here - Corteva Benefits
  • Check out life at Vylor!


Are you a good match? Apply today! We seek applicants from all backgrounds to ensure we get the best, most creative talent on our team.


The salary range for this position is $61,000.00 to $74,000.00.

Leads end‑to‑end process governance and maturity uplift

title: Body Technician (Flat Rate)
description:
NY Oneonta - 146011

We put our team members first. You’ll receive a great salary and benefits, and experience the support and opportunity you deserve. You’re empowered to make decisions. You control your future.

Job Description:

The Auto Body Technician’s primary responsibility and accountability includes providing an exceptional and successful customer experience through the meticulous assessment and quality repair of each customer’s vehicle to restore it back to pre-accident condition. The Auto Body Technician thoroughly disassembles, repairs, and reassembles each vehicle while playing a pivotal role to our company’s promise of speed, quality and customer excellence. The Auto Body Technician works in alignment with all team members in achieving the repair facilities KPIs and is committed to being a dedicated Brand Ambassador of The Boyd Group at all times.

Key Job Responsibilities

  • Ensure consistent execution of WOW (Wow Operating Way) plan.

  • Plans the repair work that is necessary and prepares cost estimates for customers. Uses various tools such as cutting guns, plasma cutters, hydraulic jacks, hammers, and pliers to repair sections of a vehicle.

  • Hammers out dents, dimples, and other minor body damage if possible; mixes and applies filler resins to repair dents when other methods are not feasible.

  • Realigns car chassis and frames to repair structural damage.

  • Removes damaged sections of vehicles and replaces them with new or aftermarket parts. Replaces or repairs glass and windshields as needed.

  • Replaces or repairs interior parts as needed.

  • Welds and otherwise attaches or fits parts into place and Prepares and repaints vehicles with factory-specified paint or agreed-upon equivalent.

  • Attempts to complete work orders within labor time guidelines. Ensures all work has been executed correctly by inspecting vehicles after repair.

  • Performs other related duties as assigned.

Education and/or Experience Required

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.

  • Successful completion of technical school program OR a 3-year apprenticeship as an auto body repairer.

Required Skills/Abilities

  • Ability to read job orders and work with very little supervision.

  • Ability to work with other repairers within an auto body shop.

  • Thorough understanding of methods and procedures to repair vehicle bodies.

  • Thorough understanding of how to use tools required for the trade.

Other Requirements

  • Must be able to work safely in a noisy area with many odors present.

  • Must be able to lift up to 30 pounds at times.

  • Must be able to visually inspect vehicle damage in a variety of weather conditions.

  • Must be able to bend, stretch, kneel, and squat to perform repairs and inspections.

Please note, this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

The physical demands of your job must be met to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the job.

Na bank cenimy sobie relacje z ludźmi. Szukamy osób, które tak jak my chcą zapewnić najlepszą jakość obsługi w sektorze finansowym - jesteśmy firmą technologiczną z usługami bankowym.

Należymy do pierwszej trójki największych banków w Polsce i jesteśmy częścią międzynarodowej Grupy Erste. Nasz dział Contact Center to ponad 1300 osób w 4 miastach w Polsce – Warszawa, Wrocław, Poznań i Lublin. Do komunikacji z klientami wykorzystujemy audio, wideo, messenger, e-mail, czat czy naszego bota.

Cenimy różnorodność wśród naszych pracowników. Wierzymy, że każdy, bez względu na indywidualne predyspozycje, może wnieść niepowtarzalną perspektywę do naszej firmy.


Aplikuj, jeśli:

  • masz pierwsze doświadczenia w budowaniu pozytywnych relacji z Klientami,
  • jesteś komunikatywny/a, gotowy/a do pomocy i nastawiony/a na cel,
  • lubisz identyfikować potrzeby klienta i reagować na nie,
  • jesteś zaangażowany/a w realizowane zadań,
  • lubisz pracować zespołowo,
  • znasz pakiet MS Office.



Twoje zadania w tej roli:

  • budowanie długofalowych relacji z Klientami, dbając o podnoszenie ich satysfakcji poprzez telefon lub chat i video,
  • promowanie i sprzedawanie produktów i usług bankowych dla Klientów MŚP,
  • realizowanie zadań sprzedażowych przy zachowaniu najwyższych standardów jakości,
  • profesjonalna obsługa posprzedażowa Klientów firmowych,
  • obsługiwanie klientów zgodnie z wymaganiami prawnymi i wymaganiami w zakresie bezpieczeństwa,
  • stosowanie najlepszych polityk banku i czynników zmniejszających ryzyko.

To masz na bank:

  • umowę o pracę,
  • pracę hybrydowa w biurze (lokalizacja na początku oferty),
  • praca zmianowa od poniedziałku do piątku w godzinach 8:00-17:00,
  • prywatną opiekę medyczną Medicover (z możliwością wykupienia pakietu stomatologicznego),
  • system kafeteryjny z punktami do wymiany na aktywności, np. wypoczynkowe, kulturalne, gastronomiczne lub dofinansowanie do przedszkola/żłobka/klubu dziecięcego,
  • kartę Multisport,
  • ofertę produktową banku oraz pożyczki na pracowniczych warunkach,
  • aktywności wellbeingowe, np. Kluby Zainteresowań, webinary, ćwiczenia, podcasty; inicjatywy w biurach np. mammobus, profilaktyczne badanie wzroku, warsztaty z samoobrony,
  • wyprawkę dla dzieci,
  • benefity dla osób z niepełnosprawnościami: dodatek finansowy na cele prozdrowotne, dodatkowe 2 dni urlopu dla pracowników z lekkim stopniem niepełnosprawności, całkowita praca zdalna, jeśli charakter pracy na to pozwala,
  • platformę ze szkoleniami zewnętrznymi i wewnętrznymi – np. programowanie czy analiza danych lub komunikacja, podejście strategiczne, negocjacje i inne,
  • program poleceń pracowniczych – nagrodę pieniężną za polecenie osoby do pracy w banku.


Jak wygląda wdrożenie i rozwój?

Na bank nie wrzucimy Cię na głęboką wodę. Zaplanowaliśmy wdrożenie, które obejmować będzie wprowadzenie do organizacji, Twojej jednostki biznesowej i zadań.
Program adaptacyjny będzie trwał około 2 miesięcy.
Na początku Twoja przełożona pokaże Ci naszą kulturę organizacyjną i odpowie na wszystkie pytania.
Po okresie wdrożenia zaczniesz pracę na planach sprzedażowych, a za ich realizację otrzymasz premię.

Dołącz do nas w kilku krokach:

  • Wyślij CV do naszej analizy, a my podejmiemy decyzję czy zaprosimy Cię do kolejnego etapu.
  • Spotkaj się (online) z managerem.
  • Wykonaj zadanie merytoryczne/test (w zależności od stanowiska).
  • Pracuj z nami w naszym zespole!


Po każdym z etapów rekrutacji otrzymasz od nas informację zwrotną, dostosowaną do jego poziomu zaawansowania. Po spotkaniach zaś wrócimy do Ciebie z kompleksowym podsumowaniem mailowym lub telefonicznym.

Stosujemy najwyższe standardy zarządzania ryzykiem, dbamy o bezpieczeństwo naszych klientów i świadczonych usług.

title: Business Analyst Lead
description:
Business Analyst Lead

London or Darlington, with hybrid working arrangements.

About the role

At Railpen, we’re committed to securing our members’ futures and delivering long-term value through effective change, innovation and continuous improvement. As Business Analyst Lead, you’ll own and develop the Business Analysis capability across Change & Transformation (C&T), while championing the profession and its value across the wider organisation.

This is a people leadership and professional capability role rather than a direct delivery position. You’ll create the conditions for Business Analysts to perform at their best through clear leadership, coaching, consistent professional standards and meaningful development opportunities. While you won’t hold direct accountability for delivering business analysis, you’ll provide guidance and constructive challenge on complex analysis activities to improve the quality, clarity and value of outputs.

Working closely with Portfolio Managers, Project Managers, Business Architecture, PMO and Resource Planning colleagues, you’ll help create the conditions for successful delivery across the change portfolio through strong capability, consistency and professional development. As a visible leader within C&T, you’ll actively contribute to team anchor days, capability forums, coaching activities, workshops and other in-person events that strengthen collaboration, professional development and community.

To learn more about Railpen including our values, culture and purpose, visit our careers page here.

What you’ll be doing

  • Line-managing and developing Business Analysts, supporting their performance, wellbeing and career progression.
  • Owning and continuously improving the Business Analysis capability, including professional standards, methodologies, frameworks, role expectations, development pathways, AI-enabled practices and ways of working.
  • Building and leading a thriving Business Analysis community that strengthens professional identity and promotes consistency, collaboration, knowledge sharing and continuous development.
  • Working with matrix managers, Portfolio Managers, Project Managers and Resource Planning colleagues to support effective deployment, utilisation, performance feedback and development of Business Analyst resource.
  • Providing people-leadership input into resourcing decisions and using performance trends, feedback and delivery insights to identify capability gaps and development priorities.
  • Coaching Business Analysts through complex analysis challenges and providing constructive challenge to improve the quality, clarity, consistency and value of outputs.
  • Driving continuous improvement in Business Analysis practice, including requirements management, process analysis, stakeholder engagement, business improvement and alignment with business architecture principles.
  • Building strong relationships with Project Management, Business Architecture and PMO leads to ensure Business Analysis standards support wider C&T delivery disciplines.
  • Promoting a consistent, professional and proportionate approach to Business Analysis across programmes, projects and smaller change initiatives.
  • Acting as a visible advocate for the Business Analysis profession across C&T and the wider organisation.

What we’re looking for

You’ll be an experienced Business Analysis and people leader with a strong track record of developing individuals, building professional capability and improving analysis practice within complex change or transformation environments. You’ll combine supportive and inclusive leadership with sound judgement and a pragmatic, proportionate approach. Comfortable working across matrix structures, you’ll build credible relationships at all levels, provide constructive challenge and translate complex business challenges into clear, actionable outcomes. You’ll use evidence, feedback and delivery insight to help Business Analysts and the wider profession continuously improve.

Essential

  • Significant experience leading Business Analysis activity within complex change, transformation or project delivery environments.
  • Proven people leadership experience, with the ability to inspire, motivate and develop high-performing teams through a collaborative and inclusive leadership style.
  • Strong coaching and mentoring capability, with the ability to adapt your approach to colleagues at different stages of their development and career journey.
  • Strong understanding of Business Analysis disciplines, including requirements management, process analysis, stakeholder engagement, business process improvement and benefits-focused change.
  • Experience establishing, implementing and continuously improving Business Analysis standards, methodologies, frameworks and ways of working.
  • Experience building and leading professional communities that promote consistency, knowledge sharing and continuous professional development.
  • The ability to provide guidance and constructive challenge on complex analysis activities, improving the quality, consistency and value of outputs.
  • Excellent stakeholder management, communication and influencing skills, with the confidence to challenge constructively and drive positive outcomes.
  • Experience working across matrix structures to support resource deployment, capability development and succession planning.
  • The ability to translate complex business challenges into clear, actionable outcomes.
  • The ability to use performance trends, feedback and delivery insight to identify capability gaps and drive continuous improvement.

Desirable

  • Experience developing or embedding AI-enabled Business Analysis practices within a change or transformation environment.
  • Experience building and leading a professional community of practice across a complex or matrix organisation.
  • Knowledge of business architecture principles and how they support effective change delivery.
  • A relevant Business Analysis qualification or professional accreditation, such as BCS or equivalent.
  • Experience within a financial services, pensions or investment environment.

Why is this role exciting now?

This is an opportunity to shape the future of the Business Analysis profession across C&T at a pivotal time. You’ll have the platform to develop talented Business Analysts, strengthen professional standards and influence the quality of analysis across a diverse portfolio of change. Rather than delivering one initiative, your impact will be seen across the Business Analysis community, helping create consistently strong capability, clearer analysis and better conditions for successful change.

What you’ll get in return

  • A competitive salary (depending on experience) plus generous annual bonus plan
  • 28 days annual leave plus bank holidays
  • We provide membership of the Railways Pension Scheme, a Defined Benefit arrangement under which you get a pension for life and a lump sum when you retire, based on your length of service and pay
  • 4x Life Assurance cover
  • We support hybrid and flexible working along with very generous family leave including 12 months full pay maternity leave and 6 months full pay paternity leave
  • Take a look at the full range of benefits available to support you, click here

Next steps

If you’re excited by the opportunity to make a meaningful contribution and grow your career with us, we encourage you to apply by 8th October

Inclusion at Railpen

At Railpen, diversity, equity and inclusion are core to who we are. We’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels respected, supported and able to thrive. Our mission to secure a better future for our members is strengthened by the different perspectives and experiences our people bring.

We are transparent about our gender pay gap and are actively committed to addressing it through fair and inclusive recruitment, progression and reward practices.

We respect and support individuals’ pronouns and encourage colleagues to share them if they feel comfortable to do so.

We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and do not discriminate on the basis of age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, neurodiversity, or any other protected characteristic. If you need adjustments during the recruitment process, just let us know.

Whether you're supporting business operations, coordinating projects, or helping teams work more efficiently, you'll contribute to continuous improvement, deliver exceptional service, and help build a more agile, connected, and innovative business.

Guided by our purpose of making the benefits of technology accessible to all, we provide expertise, solutions, and connections that help shape what's next. As a global technology solutions provider, Arrow offers opportunities to learn, collaborate, and build a meaningful career while making an impact around the world.

Life at Arrow

title: Logistics Account Supervisor
